title: Web routing, request validation, and handler boundaries
sources: Python documentation: dictionaries, exceptions, and HTTP-client concepts
HTTP semantics concepts: request methods, status codes, and representation boundaries
masterChecklist: Framework survey and project labs: Flask/FastAPI/Django concepts; use one verified framework version per deep module
HTTP methods, status codes, headers, request/response bodies and API contracts
Input validation, serialization, error design, pagination and versioning
whyItMatters: A web handler is a public boundary. It must turn untrusted request data into a clear domain call and return a stable response without mixing routing, storage, and business rules.
simpleExplanation: Routing chooses a handler for a method and path. The handler validates input, calls a domain service, and maps the result to a response. Framework syntax differs, but these responsibilities are transferable.
mentalModel: A handler is a receptionist: it checks the form, sends a clear request to the right specialist, and returns an understandable answer rather than letting visitors wander into the back office.
outcomes: Separate route, validation, domain rule, and response.

realWorldExample.scenario: A client marks a lesson complete.
realWorldExample.riskWithoutSetup: The handler trusts raw input and exposes an exception.
realWorldExample.professionalApproach: Validate the lesson ID, call a service, and return a documented success or safe error shape.

explanation: The handler validates untrusted shape before domain work.
The service is injected, so routing/framework code does not own business logic.
The returned status/body is an explicit contract.
workedExample.expectedOutput: Invalid input yields a 400-style response; valid input yields a success body.
workedExample.safeExperiment: Return the raw exception instead and identify the privacy and usability risk.

procedure: Match route/method to a small handler.
Call a domain service through a narrow boundary.
Map expected errors to documented responses.
Test normal, invalid, and denied cases.

commonMistakes.mistake: Putting database calls and request parsing in every route.
commonMistakes.avoid: Keep a handler thin and delegate domain/storage work.

commonMistakes.why: They expose internals and confuse users.
commonMistakes.avoid: Return safe errors and log controlled diagnostics.

commonMistakes.mistake: Changing a response field without checking consumers.
commonMistakes.why: Clients may parse the existing contract.
commonMistakes.avoid: Version or migrate the response deliberately.

lab.title: Model a safe completion handler
lab.solutionExplanation: The handler validates at the boundary and returns a documented status/body. A real framework supplies routing syntax but not the design decision.
challenges: Find the bug: calling strip before checking for str.
Experiment: add an ownership check through a service.

projectConnection.milestone: Create one thin handler around a validated domain call.
projectConnection.definitionOfDone: Normal, invalid, and denied behavior are documented and tested.
